newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs up on firmer cash ideas, spread unwinding.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs up on firmer cash ideas, spread unwinding.

text.p: Expectations that cash pork and live markets are near a bottom supported CME hog futures with unwinding of bear spreads adding to gains by the close. Pork bellies followed hogs as short covering offset early commercial resistance, traders said.
Hog futures closed 0.675 cent higher to 0.025 lower with April up most at 70.100 cents. Pork bellies ended 0.900 to 0.600 higher with May up 0.850 at 75.975 cents.
Mixed demand and spread action pushed April hog futures up into buy stops early. Talk continued of increased interest for pork items at the lower price levels, traders said.

Although loins remained weak in the noon USDA report, other cuts were generally steady. Number two pork cutout values had slipped to $66.41 per cwt Thursday, the lowest price level since April 8, 1996 and this should prompt some retailer interest, they said.
The latest CME lean hog index was also up $0.37 to $67.60 per cwt.

Early talk on the Pig Crop report due later in the month also lent support to the nearby. Hog numbers could be unchanged from a year ago. However, expectations of herd expansion kept a lid on deferred months, they added.

ABN Chicogo Corp actively spread long April/short June with Cargill Investor Services, R.J. O'Brien and Rand Financials also doing the spread later. Refco and Rand were on both sides of April early with Refco also spreading long June/short April. Lind-Waldock bought April and R.J. O'Brien sold June early, pit sources said.
In hog options, Lind-Waldock bought the April 66/73 strangle and bought August 72 puts. Volatility was up in August and firm in other months, pit sources added.
Pork bellies followed the lead of hogs and moved up on local and mixed commission house short covering.
A steady tone to cash bellies at noon again encouraged ideas the cash market was near a bottom. Stopping of deliveries by strong hands added to support, they said.
However, commercial selling had limited early gains. Concern remained over the recent increases in storage stocks, they added.
Rand, ABN Chicogo Corp, LFG and locals bought early while R.J. O'Brien, LIT division of First Options and Prudential Securities sold, pit sources said.
